2.text: with cudgels; for instance, black shamans caught while working spells. In

3.text: the region of Dawn abide the “bloody ones” (moʟɪˊyñɪt); that is, all killed

4.text: with sharp weapons, especially those who were killed at their own request.

5.text: Deceased women who have no husbands go to a world of their own.

6.text: They live there, catching reindeer with nooses and nets as they come to

7.text: cross Pebbly River. Their world is situated in the lower portion of the sky,

8.text: and it is much less important than the first upper world.

9.text: While some of the dead are in these

10.text: upper worlds, the usual place of abode for

11.text: the deceased is underground. Their country

12.text: is very extensive, and full of intricate paths

13.text: which puzzle new-comers. The sketch Fig.

14.text: 236 represents the paths in the world of the

15.text: dead as they are claimed to have been seen,

16.text: in a deep swoon, by the man who drew it.

17.text: The circular marks represent holes through

18.text: which new-comers enter. The smallest of

19.text: them are intended for those who died by

21.text: A new-comer to the world of the dead

22.text: has to pass at first through a region inhabited

23.text: by dogs, who live in small earth huts of their

24.text: own. Men who during their lives were unkind

25.text: to dogs, and habitually beat them, will be attacked by the dogs underground,

26.text: and bitten severely.¹ The forefathers and relatives of a new-comer meet
